name: Masala Omelette
cuisine: Pan-Indian (home kitchens, Irani cafés, dhabas and Mumbai omelette-pav carts)

ingredients.name: Onion (pyaz/kanda)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ small onion, very finely chopped (about 3 tbsp)

ingredients.name: Tomato (tamatar)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ medium tomato, seeds removed, very finely chopped (about 2 tbsp)

ingredients.name: Groundnut oil (or any neutral cooking oil)

equipment: 8-inch (20 cm) frying pan or tawa, ideally non-stick
Flat, wide spatula (wooden or silicone is gentlest)
Chopping board and a sharp knife
Measuring spoons (normal teaspoons are a fine stand-in)

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Peel and very finely chop 30 g (¼ small) onion.
steps.tip: Hold the onion's flat cut side down so it does not roll.
steps.visualCue: Tiny, even pieces, smaller than a lentil; about 3 tbsp on the board.
steps.cameraCheck: About 3 tbsp chopped onion on the board
steps.videoShot: The knife rocking through the onion.
steps.watchOut: Big chunks. The omelette cooks in about 3 minutes, so large pieces stay raw and crunchy and tear the omelette when you flip. If you see pieces bigger than a lentil, chop them again.

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Cut ¼ tomato, scoop out the seeds and watery pulp with a spoon, and very finely chop the flesh (25 g).
steps.visualCue: Small red cubes with no loose seeds and no pooled juice on the board.
steps.videoShot: The spoon scooping out the seeds, then the knife dicing.
steps.watchOut: Leaving the seeds in. The extra juice makes the omelette soggy and slow to set. If the board is wet with juice, pat the tomato dry with a paper towel.

steps.title: Chop the chilli and coriander
steps.text: Very finely chop ½ green chilli (3 g) and 1 tbsp (3 g) coriander leaves.
steps.visualCue: Fine green flecks; the coriander smells fresh and the chilli smells sharp.
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped chilli and coriander side by side
steps.watchOut: Touching your eyes after cutting the chilli. Stinging fingers are the sign; wash your hands with soap, not just water. Take out the chilli seeds if you want it milder.

steps.title: Crack the eggs
steps.text: Crack 2 eggs into the bowl, one at a time.
steps.tip: Crack on a flat surface rather than the bowl rim for fewer shell bits.
steps.visualCue: Two whole yolks in the bowl, no shell pieces.
steps.videoShot: An egg cracking on the counter and opening into the bowl.
steps.watchOut: Shell fragments, which show as small white or brown specks in the egg. Lift them out with a larger piece of the shell, which works better than a finger.

steps.title: Add salt and spices
steps.text: Add the salt (a big pinch, 1 g), a pinch of turmeric (0.25 g) and ¼ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder (0.5 g).
steps.visualCue: Small yellow and red heaps sitting on top of the egg.
steps.cameraCheck: The spices sitting on the eggs
steps.videoShot: The spices sprinkled into the bowl.
steps.watchOut: Too much turmeric, which makes the omelette taste bitter and look orange-brown. A pinch is only what fits between two fingertips; if you tipped in a spoonful, add one more egg to dilute it.

steps.title: Beat the eggs
steps.text: Beat with a fork until fully mixed (add the optional 1 tbsp milk now if you want it).
steps.tip: Tilt the bowl and whisk briskly; the air you beat in makes the omelette fluffier.
steps.visualCue: An even golden-yellow mix with a light froth on top and no streaks of white.
steps.cameraCheck: The beaten eggs in the bowl
steps.videoShot: The fork whisking in quick circles.
steps.watchOut: Streaks of clear egg white. They cook into rubbery white patches. If you see them, beat for 10 more seconds.

steps.title: Mix in the vegetables
steps.text: Add the onion, tomato, chilli and coriander to the eggs and stir to combine.
steps.visualCue: Colourful flecks spread evenly through the egg, not sunk in one heap at the bottom.
steps.cameraCheck: The speckled egg mix in the bowl
steps.videoShot: The fork folding the vegetables in.
steps.watchOut: Vegetables sinking to the bottom while you heat the pan. The omelette then has a bare half. Give the bowl one more stir right before pouring.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Put the pan on medium heat. Add 1½ tsp (7.5 ml) oil and tilt the pan to coat the base.
steps.visualCue: The oil looks thin and shimmery and spreads easily; a drop of egg dropped in sizzles at once.
steps.cameraCheck: The oiled pan on the flame
steps.watchOut: Smoking oil, which means the pan is too hot and the omelette will brown before the inside sets. If you see smoke, take the pan off the heat for 20 seconds and lower the flame.

steps.title: Pour in the eggs
steps.text: Stir the egg mix once more, then pour it into the pan. Tilt the pan so it spreads into an even circle.
steps.tip: Nudge any bunched vegetables flat with the spatula tip.
steps.visualCue: A gentle sizzle, and an even layer about ½ cm thick reaching close to the pan edge.
steps.cameraCheck: The egg spread across the pan
steps.videoShot: The speckled egg pouring in and spreading.
steps.watchOut: A fierce, spitting sizzle with edges browning immediately means the pan is too hot. Lower the flame at once. A thick, small omelette means the pan is too small; it will stay wet in the middle.

steps.title: Let it set
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium-low. Leave it untouched.
steps.visualCue: The edges turn opaque and matte and lift slightly from the pan; the top is mostly set with only a thin shiny wet layer left.
steps.videoShot: Close-up of the edges going from glossy to matte.
steps.watchOut: Poking or stirring now, which turns it into scrambled egg. Leave it alone. If the top stays very wet after 2 minutes, cover the pan with a lid for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Loosen the edges
steps.text: Run the spatula around the edge and under the omelette.
steps.visualCue: The omelette slides freely when you shake the pan gently.
steps.videoShot: The omelette gliding as the pan is shaken.
steps.watchOut: Sticking in one spot, which tears the omelette at the flip. Slide the spatula under that spot and add a few drops of oil at the edge.

steps.title: Flip it
steps.text: Slide the wide spatula under the middle and turn the omelette over in one quick move.
steps.tip: Or use the plate trick from the Equipment list.
steps.visualCue: The cooked side is golden with a few light brown spots.
steps.watchOut: Raw liquid egg running out when you lift it, a sign it needed another 20 seconds to set. Put it back down, wait, and try again. If it tears, press the pieces together; it tastes the same.

steps.title: Cook the second side
steps.visualCue: No wet egg at the edges; pressed lightly in the centre it feels springy, not liquid.
steps.cameraCheck: The omelette in the pan, second side down
steps.videoShot: The spatula pressing the centre gently.
steps.watchOut: A dark brown, dry underside, which means the heat was too high; the omelette turns rubbery. Take it off earlier next time.

steps.title: Fold and plate
steps.text: Fold the omelette in half (optional) and slide it onto a plate.
steps.visualCue: Golden outside, soft and moist inside, with red, white and green flecks.
steps.videoShot: The omelette sliding onto the plate, then a fork cutting into it.
steps.watchOut: Leaving it in the hot pan, where it keeps cooking and dries out. Plate it straight away.

reasons: two whole eggs give about 13 g of complete protein for about 225 kcal, with only 1½ tsp oil and a quick pan-cook. Onion, tomato, chilli and coriander add flavour and a little fibre and vitamin C. Points come off for the cholesterol (about 370 mg) and saturated fat in the yolks and for low fibre. Café and street versions often use a tablespoon or more of butter, more salt, and almost always come with buttered pav or white bread, which can double the calories.

researchRating.basis: a staple everyday Indian egg dish. Recipe pages rate it highly but with small vote counts: Whisk Affair 4.86/5 (7 votes, updated Jan 2026), Cup of Yum 5.0 (21 reviews), Champagne Tastes 5/5 (5 votes), Marks & Spencer 5/5 (3 ratings), Caroline's Cooking 5/5 (2 votes), Yummy Tummy 4/5 (1 vote), Cookbooker (Madhur Jaffrey version) 4.0/5 (1 review); Tesco's recipe has 135 ratings but the average was not visible. Small deduction because vote counts are small and it is seen as a basic dish rather than a standout one. Compared with the previous version, the sources and the score both hold up at 4.5.

storage: Best eaten fresh. Fridge-safe in an airtight box within 2 hours of cooking, for up to 2 days, though it turns rubbery after day 1. Freezing is not recommended (watery and spongy when thawed). Reheat in a pan on low with a lid for 1–2 min per side, or microwave covered in 15-second bursts until hot all through.
leftoverRemix: Omelette egg-fried rice ("omelette pulao"). Slice the cold omelette into strips. Heat ½ tsp oil, add 1 cup cooked rice, a pinch of salt, ¼ tsp pepper and ½ tsp soy sauce, toss 2 min. Fold in the strips and a handful of spring onion greens, toss 30 sec more.
burnOff: about 3.2 km of running (225 ÷ 70 kcal/km, 70 kg adult) or about 4.5 km of brisk walking (about 55 min at 5 km/h, about 50 kcal/km) (est.). With 2 buttered pav (about 465 kcal): about 6.6 km running or 9.3 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: egg, onion and table salt are all avoided in vrat (most common rule set assumed)

ekadashi.reason: egg and onion are avoided on Ekadashi

ramadan.reason: egg is halal; about 13 g protein for about 225 kcal keeps you full at sehri (pair with a roti; salt is moderate at about 1 g)

jain.reason: contains egg and onion (egg is not Jain; onion is a root vegetable)

vegan.reason: contains egg (and ghee/milk if the optional versions are used)

pescatarian.reason: eggs are allowed in a pescatarian diet; no meat

sattvik.reason: contains onion and egg; dropping onion would still leave egg, which is not sattvik

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, rava, maida or hing in the recipe (do not add compounded hing, which usually contains wheat flour)

dairyFree.reason: cooked in oil; the optional 1 tbsp milk and any ghee or butter are left out

variants.reason: egg and onion are both outside Jain rules, and the dish is defined by egg.
the dish is defined by egg; an eggless chickpea-flour version is a different dish (see dish 16, Besan Chilla).
main recipe already gluten-free (no hing; do not use compounded hing).
main recipe already dairy-free (oil, no milk, ghee or butter).
